label: D2 after a common a1 -> S1 transition
explanation: Fires only at DELAY_2 when the agent chose a1 and reached S1 (the common transition for a1), i.e. the conjunction of the last-action input a1 and the state input S1. It is silent at D1 and GO, on a1 -> S2 (rare), a2 -> S1 (rare) and a2 -> S2 (common). Dev split P = R = F1 = 1.0 and correlation 0.999. Both variables are observed at D2, so no future variable is used. The state input alone (D2 & S1) reaches only F1 0.83 because it also includes rare a2 -> S1 trials. Magnitude is almost binary (median 3.23, max 3.50). The small variation runs a little higher in the top windows, which come from long runs of rewarded a1 choices (high-value bin), but I did not test magnitude modulation in detail.

issues: No issues found. On the test split the predicate (phase == D2) & (action == 1) & (state == 1) scores precision 1.0, recall 1.0, F1 1.0, mass recall 1.0 and correlation 0.9993, with exactly 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.

The claims check out. Dev profile: 0 activations at D1 and GO, all activation mass at D2, and in_action == 1 and in_state == 1 each carry 100% of the mass. The predicate also covers every activation quartile.

Ablations agree with the explanation. On the test split D2 & S1 alone reaches F1 0.823 (it adds rare a2 -> S1 trials) and D2 & a1 alone reaches F1 0.850 (it adds rare a1 -> S2 trials). The full conjunction is needed.

The magnitude is close to binary (mean 3.233, median 3.225, max 3.504) and the correlation is 0.999, so there is no meaningful graded modulation left to explain. The predicate uses no future variables.
